label: 2026-09-06 manual-worker insanity point
population_semantics: manual runs are assigned by started_at; archive time never moves an old-format run across the boundary; post-change sanity evidence accumulates from the fixed boundary until this baseline is explicitly superseded

score_semantics.component_formula: weight * clamp((baseline-current)/baseline, -1, 1); all scored components are lower-is-better
score_semantics.important: Diagnostic behavior trend only. Report size/verbosity is never scored. Go/continue duration stays a separate continuation projection. Never a worker target, completion gate, scheduler input, product acceptance signal, or run-length incentive.
score_semantics.headline_formula: operational lifecycle delta only; reporting-shape diagnostics are excluded from the headline

guardrails: General manual sanity headline scores lifecycle/process behavior only; report size and transcript-field count are diagnostic and cannot raise or lower the headline.
Reporting diagnostics remain visible to detect overhead regressions without turning brevity into an optimization target.
Continuation/go duration and fragmentation are reported separately from bounded manual task durations; never use the mixed manual population to answer whether `go` runs are too short.
Do not claim continuation improvement before the continuation sample gate is met.
The score measures manual execution/report lifecycle behavior, not model intelligence, user wellbeing, product quality, or MCP health.

operational.semantics: Measures explicit lifecycle mistakes across actual manual execution runs. This is the only current headline axis because it reflects behavior rather than report verbosity.

reporting.semantics: Diagnostic reporting overhead only. Report bytes and transcript-field count are retained for observability but have zero influence on the sanity headline.

continuation_baseline.source_semantics: Six hours before PR #658, using only historical manual reports explicitly identifiable as go/continue from run_id or scope; bounded historical subset, not all manual work.
continuation_baseline.important: Separate from the general manual sanity score. Do not infer go/continue quality from bounded one-shot task or correction durations; user-interrupted continuation runs should be identified by stop_reason when available.

machine_lifecycle_diagnostic.important: Machine-classified terminalization is stronger than self-reported anomaly text, but the reconciler was introduced after the fixed #658 baseline. Pre-instrumentation snapshots are survivor-biased, so this stays diagnostic-only until a comparable prospective baseline exists.
